messages.subject: Question about balance measures for categorical covariates
messages.subject_clean: Question about balance measures for categorical covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have been using MatchIt for a project and have some categorical
covariates. (I know that continuous covariates are optimal, but
unfortunately we only have categorical for some of our data). I have
already coded them so that the categories are numeric.

When I perform the matching and ask for the summary, sometimes it gives
balance measures for all of the levels of the categorical variable and
other times it does not. For example, my variable Class Standing is 4
levels and I get balance measures for all 4 levels, but my variable Current
GPA is 4 levels and I only get balance measures for the second, third, and
fourth level of the variable.

Is there a way to correct this?

Thank you,
Maureen Bowers

messages.body_plain:
Use the *cobalt *package, which interfaces directly with *MatchIt *output.
bal.tab(m.out), where m.out is the output of a call to matchit(), produces
a balance table like summary() but solves some of these issues. Binary
variables will have one level displayed, while multi-category variables
will have all levels displayed. Note the default balance statistic for
binary variables is the raw difference in proportion, but the option to
produce standardized difference is available.

I'm not sure why that glitch occurs in *MatchIt*. Nothing about the raw
code seems to imply that this might occur except if you have an unusual
variable name that uses spaces or other punctuations.

Noah

PS, full disclosure, I am the author of *cobalt*.

messages.body_plain:
Actually, I did find the issue. The first factor variable provided in the
formula should have all levels represented, while the other factor
variables will have their first level removed. This has to do with how the
matchit code process the input formula (lines 46-49 in the matchit.R
script).

Noah
